summary: Keep the glossary's I classification and mdayšalle/mdayšən base forms. Initial m- does not justify reassigning the verb to III, nor is it dyš 'run over'.
Preterit mdayšalle/-alli/-alla shows n+l assimilation; plural mdayšanne contrasts with Infectum mdayšni. The mismatch in inherited 75/16–17 is corrected without changing the wording.

Sense 1 covers onset of activities: b- with transport, occupation, bread preparation, boasting or singing; l- with crying or calls for help; ʕal with conversation. These are productive complements, not distinct idioms or numbered senses.

66/285 contains both lu hawar (begun activity) and li aṯto (l-marked agent). 96/61 combines target aʕla and stones bak kefe; this does not establish a separate 'attack' sense when onset of the contextually specified activity suffices.

Narrative Infectum can describe onset, while the German edition uses a past tense. Repeated crying in consecutive Mor Barsaumo verses supplies no new box or sense. Same-source quotations in Hors/EL and JL are not counted twice.

Round 2 only. Jan English is a project machine translation, not an edition translation; all semantic decisions rest on the Turoyo. Round-1 proposals are inherited in the reading layout and are not repeated in this JSON.

Jan adds a directive mdayšən in a permission quote. Adjacent Jan 4.II/797 concerns continuing at university and becoming a teacher; /799 confirms parental permission. This supports begin with the activity omitted.
The entry’s I allocation and sense 1 are retained. The new Imperativ box is based on one elliptical quotation; gender-specific morphology is not inferred from the addressee.
Confirm the relocation of inherited 75/16–17 to Infectum against the editors' paradigm; the supplied 3pl form lacks the Preterit agent suffix.
Does 96/61 lexicalize attacking, or is it ordinary anfangen with a target and an omitted throwing activity? Current evidence supports the latter and does not add a sense.
Confirm the audible ending and Imperativ paradigm of mdayšən (Jan 4.II/798), addressed to a woman. Is a final vowel clipped, or is this a bare Infectum used as a directive?
The animate subject can be an animal (the horse begins crying). Activity complements may be overt action nouns, an occupation/project, or omitted when recoverable.
